transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-14 16:00 PST / Duration: ~58 minutes / Attendees: Sofia, Marco, Aisha (Redwood); Dana, Evan, Priya, Oliver (Crestline)

Summary: Quick results review from pilot week 3, finalize canary thresholds, lock cutover runbook and escalation path, align on who owns which play for the go/no-go rehearsal. Some discussion on VPC peering, KMS integration, and whether to do A/B 10% ramp vs. canary 1%.

[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining — we have about an hour— we'll run through the last week of telemetry, then go into the cutover runbook and roles, and end with next steps.
[00:18] Dana Morales: Thanks Sofia — quick note, we had a couple of duplicate user prompts in week 3, so we want that fixed before production.
[00:27] Marco Li: Yeah I saw that in the sample traces, looks like a cache priming edge-case, the KV cash — uh KV cache — wasn't warmed for a subset of flows. We'll propose a priming step in the runbook.
[00:40] Evan Tsu: For context, our staging traffic is synthetic ramped to 20% of peak. We can push higher if you need.
[00:48] Marco Li: That'd be great. For the canary we'll need a sustained run to see latency tail behavior.
[00:56] Priya Shah: Security - quick question, are we still planning to route through Crestline KMS or Redwood-managed key for token encryption?
[01:06] Sofia Patel: Good call. We outlined two options in the spreadsheet: VPC + customer KMS (preferred by security) or customer-managed keys via our HSM integration. We'll add the exact checklist.
[01:18] Dana Morales: Our success criteria for go-live is sub-150ms p50 and p99 under 600ms for typical 512 token prompts, and no untriaged fidelity regressions vs baseline.
[01:30] Marco Li: Re: p99 we saw 580ms in the peak load last night but that was with cold KV cache for some flows. After the priming patch it's down closer to 420ms. I'll paste the run artifacts to the shared sheet.
[01:44] Oliver Kent: I also want to confirm the fail-open plan: if Redwood Dedicated nodes are transiently unavailable, do we have a fallback model?
[01:52] Tom Boyle: Yes. We recommended automatic fallback to a smaller model in a neighboring region per the routing matrix. The runbook includes a region-failover block and cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:05] Evan Tsu: Are there any surprises around egress bandwidth or NAT gateway limits when we run the sustained test? We hit NAT throttling before.
[02:14] Marco Li: Good call. Increase NAT throughput and we'll throttle at the load-generator side to mimic production. We should also test with compressed payloads.

--- Results review (quick) ---
[02:40] Sofia Patel: OK results — week 3 summary: 3 regressions flagged, 2 infra-led latency events, 1 prompt-processing mismatch. We triaged two already. Marco, you had the list?
[02:52] Marco Li: Yup. Regression A: tokenizer mismatch on multi-byte chars — fix merged. Regression B: beam sampler path gave slightly different completions — we reverted candidate sampling to previous config for the test. Latency event was due to underprovisioned batch workers during a burst.
[03:10] Dana Morales: The reverted sampling fixed the fidelity delta in our eval set. We ran A/B on a small slice and human evals showed parity.
[03:19] Sofia Patel: Great. So main outstanding is the runbook and telemetry thresholds.

--- Cutover runbook discussion ---
[03:35] Sofia Patel: Walkthrough step-by-step — pre-cutover checks, canary plan, monitoring gates, rollback. We'll go stage by stage and call out owners.
[03:44] Marco Li: Pre-cutover: KV-cache priming run, NSG and route verification, canary config pushed (traffic-split), and synthetic user flows executed.
[03:55] Dana Morales: For canary we were thinking 1% for first 15 minutes then 5% for 30 minutes then 25% if all gates green. Alternative is A/B 10% vs control for a longer period to check fidelity.
[04:08] Priya Shah: Security would prefer slower ramp — gives time to validate logs and SIEM alerts. Also need SAML assertion logs matched for SSO.
[04:17] Tom Boyle: The runbook we propose: Canary ramp 1 -> 5 -> 10 over 45 minutes, with automatic rollback triggers on these metrics: p50 > 200ms above baseline, p99 > 800ms, error rate > 0.8%, or fidelity regression score drop > 3 points on eval set.
[04:35] Dana Morales: Can we tie the fidelity regression trigger to the feature flags so we can quickly revert model variant?
[04:42] Marco Li: Yes, we'll keep the model pinned under a rollout config and use the feature flag to toggle.
[04:47] Evan Tsu: For the rollback, who runs the actual toggle?
[04:50] Sofia Patel: By default Marco will execute the toggle, with Evan and Oliver on standby to revert network changes. Priya will confirm security posture post-rollback. We'll capture this as a play in the runbook.

--- Telemetry and alerts ---
[05:10] Marco Li: Telemetry we care about: per-route latency histograms, per-account token burn, model fidelity eval set score, user-facing error counts, and KV cache hit ratio. Recommended thresholds are in the sheet.
[05:22] Sofia Patel: We also want a synthetic smoke alert: if 3 consecutive smoke health-checks fail, trigger an incident channel. Who owns on-call?
[05:30] Oliver Kent: Crestline SRE will own first-line. Redwood will be second-line until Day 7 post-cutover.
[05:36] Aisha Rahman: We'll provide an oncall twilio hook and the runbook play for escalation.

--- VPC/KMS and compliance ---
[06:00] Priya Shah: Security specific asks: KMS key rotation proof, audit log retention (90 days min), and SSO integration with Okta. Also SOC2 in place?
[06:11] Sofia Patel: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO in our security pack; we'll share the redacted artifacts. For KMS we support customer-managed keys; we'll add the configuration steps to the runbook.
[06:23] Priya Shah: Please include the exact API endpoints for key exchange and the times when key rotation would be scheduled — we cannot rotate during the two-hour window after cutover.
[06:31] Sofia Patel: Noted.

--- Canary vs A/B discussion ---
[06:45] Dana Morales: The tradeoff: canary gives fast safety but less statistical confidence on fidelity; A/B gives better statistical power but longer exposure. Our app can start with canary then follow with a short A/B slice.
[06:58] Tom Boyle: That's a good hybrid approach: 1% -> 10% canary then 10% A/B for 24h on a sample of low-risk traffic. We'll document sample size and confidence intervals.
[07:11] Evan Tsu: Any cost implications for the A/B hold? We need to estimate token burn and model compute.
[07:18] Sofia Patel: We'll include projected unit cost for a 24-hour A/B at 10% in the pricing addendum.

--- Runbook rehearsal and roles ---
[07:30] Sofia Patel: Rehearsal plan: dry-run on Tue 05/19 at 10:00 PST. Marco will execute priming and toggle, Evan will validate network, Priya will run security checklist, Dana will observe fidelity metrics, Sofia will coordinate and call go/no-go.
[07:47] Dana Morales: Can we have a shorter blackout window to test rollback? We prefer a 10-minute circuit-breaker test in staging.
[07:55] Marco Li: We can simulate circuit breaker but we'll run it in staging first. The runbook will show manual and automated rollback steps.

--- Edge cases and miscellaneous ---
[08:12] Oliver Kent: What about multi-region reads? If we failover, do we have cross-region cache warmers?
[08:18] Marco Li: We have a cross-region cache seeding job; it's in the ops appendix. We'll run it as part of pre-cutover.
[08:25] Priya Shah: Legal wants to confirm data residency for EU pilot later — can that be scoped separately?
[08:29] Sofia Patel: Yes, we can gate EU migration as a follow-up pilot. This go-live is NA only.

--- Link references shared during call ---
[08:45] Sofia Patel: Links I'll share after: cutover runbook (https://redwood.app/pilot-runbooks/crestline-cutover), telemetry sheet (https://redwood.app/sheets/crestline-telemetry), security pack (https://redwood.app/security/crestline-pack).

--- Final recap and explicit next steps ---
[09:05] Sofia Patel: Recap — lock threshold values (Marco), schedule rehearsal Tue 05/19 (Sofia to send invite), send security docs (Sofia/Priya), run extended staging load (Marco/Evan), and finalize cutover runbook with owners.
[09:20] Dana Morales: Sounds good. We'll confirm SRE on-call rotation for the rehearsal.
[09:26] Priya Shah: I'll look over the security snippets and send outstanding Qs.
[09:31] Aisha Rahman: I'll create the incident channel and add the Twilio hook.
[09:38] Sofia Patel: Excellent. Any other items?
[09:42] Speaker 1 - contract note: quick note, procurement might require an addendum for dedicated capacity burst credit.
[09:49] Sofia Patel: We'll add pricing note.

Close: thanks everybody — we'll share the runbook and the action item list after the call.

--- END TRANSCRIPT ---

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mis-attribution, small filler words and repeated phrases, product names sometimes lowercased or split (redwood dedicate / KV cash).
